tasks.title: Choose which Ollama model is in use, without breaking the licence gate

`orchestrator ollama --use <model>` sets the active model, persisted somewhere committed and readable - company/state/company_state.json is the existing place for runtime state and already carries ollama_status.
--use REFUSES a model that is not APPROVED in the registry. Call the existing require_approved(); do not add a second licence check that could drift from it.

--use REFUSES a model that does not fit in RAM, naming the model size and the machine's total. gemma4:26b is 17.33 GB against 15.71 GB and must be refused on those grounds even if someone later marks it APPROVED - installed, licensed and unloadable are three separate things.

Both refusals exit non-zero and say which of the three checks failed. A refusal that does not say why sends someone to change the wrong thing.

Tests, with the HTTP layer injected as the existing ones do: --use accepts an approved model that fits; refuses an unapproved one; refuses an oversized one; refuses one that is not installed; and the persisted choice survives a reload.
notes: Read ollama_client.py fully first. list_models(), approved_models() and require_approved() already exist and the local-only guard (NonLocalEndpointRefused) must stay - do not widen it.
hardware.py already has model_fit() and ollama_model_sizes. Use them rather than re-deriving sizes.

tasks.title: Every orchestrator run leaves a committed log, so failures reach Claude without copy-paste
tasks.goal: Unity compile errors and build results already reach Claude on their own: sync-and-run.ps1 commits Reports/errors/latest.txt and Reports/build-status/latest.txt every 15 minutes and Claude reads them from the fork. Orchestrator runs have no such channel - when `team run` or `serve` or `codex --doctor` fails, the output dies on the PC console and the human has to retype it into a chat window. acceptance: A new module company/orchestrator/runlog.py writes one file per orchestrator run under Reports/runs/, plus Reports/runs/latest.txt holding the most recent one. Follow the shape of the two files that already work - read Reports/errors/latest.txt and Reports/build-status/latest.txt first and match their heading style, because Claude parses those and a third format is a third parser.

Each entry records: UTC timestamp, the subcommand and its arguments, the exit code, how long it took, and the tail of stdout/stderr (cap the tail - a Unity build log must not land in git). A run that raised records the exception type and message.
It records FAILURES as loudly as successes. A run that ends non-zero, raises, or times out is the entire point of this task; a log that only contains successes is worse than none.
main.py wires it into every subcommand through ONE place, not by editing each cmd_* function. The dispatcher already calls args.func(args) - wrap that call.

SECRETS: no value of any key in policy blocked_env_keys, and no value of the env var named by gemini_api_key_env, may ever be written. Reuse the existing 'names only' idiom - CodexRunner.stripped_keys - do not write a second redaction path that can drift from it. A test asserts a key value placed in the environment does not appear in the written file.
The log directory is bounded: keep at most 50 entries, delete the oldest beyond that. This is committed to git, so unbounded growth is a repository problem, not just a disk one.

sync-and-run.ps1 commits Reports/runs/ alongside the two reports it already commits. It must stay ASCII-only - Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 in the local codepage and Korean literals break parsing. That is not a style preference, it has already broken this exact file once.

Writing the log NEVER changes the outcome of the command. If the log cannot be written (read-only disk, missing directory, permission error), the run still returns its real exit code and the failure to log is reported on stderr and nowhere else. A logging bug that turns a passing build into a failure would be worse than the problem this task solves.

Tests: a successful run writes an entry; a non-zero run writes one saying so; a raising run writes one naming the exception; a secret in the environment never appears in the file; the 50-entry cap evicts oldest-first; a write failure does not change the returned exit code.
